title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: arXiv 2611.01976 'The Tool Update Gap': malicious tool updates hit 97.6% attack success across 7 agent frameworks, Claude Code included
bullets.summary: The ETUDE attack hides malicious code inside updates to tools an agent already trusts; because the code runs outside the model's context, in-context prompt-injection defenses miss it. It reached 97.6% attack success while still completing 95.9% of legitimate tasks across Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Claude Code and four other frameworks, and the authors say existing defenses are insufficient.
bullets.how: The Construct: pin versions of every MCP server, plugin and skill, and re-review on update instead of auto-trusting new versions; the unattended loops are exactly the setting this attack targets. PRAGMA: 'tool supply-chain review' is a concrete client security offer. Brand 9 Signs: applies through the shop and ops agents.

bullets.title: Claude Code 2.1.323: experimental Code Mode (Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools) + plugin version-range gating
bullets.summary: First seen Nov 13: an opt-in Code Mode where Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools rather than issuing one tool call at a time; plugin.json now accepts engines["claude-code"] to gate a plugin to supported Claude Code versions; and managed settings add CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL for Claude Desktop on third-party providers.
bullets.how: The Construct: trial Code Mode on multi-step tool chains (render, publish, order loops) and compare tokens per successful task; add engines version ranges to the Construct and b9 plugins so they don't break silently on upgrade. PRAGMA: a cost lever to show clients. Brand 9 Signs: indirect.

bullets.title: Anthropic (Nov 12): self-hosted Claude Managed Agents in private beta + Claude for Manufacturing plugin
bullets.summary: Managed Agents can now run the full service, including harness, sandboxes, credentials and session history, in a customer's own cloud or on-prem, with the customer choosing where model requests go (access via the Anthropic account team). Separately, Claude for Manufacturing ships as a plugin with 17 skills and connectors for Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365 and Oracle NetSuite on Team and Enterprise.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: self-hosted agents remove the data-residency objection for regulated or cautious clients, and the Manufacturing plugin is a template for packaging a vertical as skills + connectors. Brand 9 Signs: the Fusion connector is worth a look for CNC/fabrication work. The Construct: no need to self-host today.

bullets.title: Kindo raises $30M (total $57.6M) for enterprise AI-agent control
bullets.summary: Announced Nov 12, co-led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, to expand go-to-market and its AI Control Center and Deep Hat models (Sift event filtering, Tune small-model adaptation, Shrink workflow steps as code, Attack authorized security testing); Kindo reports about 800% year-over-year revenue growth.
bullets.how: PRAGMA: agent control and governance keeps drawing security-led money, which supports a governance line in the operator offer. The Construct: its 'Shrink' idea (turn repeated agent steps into code) matches Code Mode and is worth applying to stable loops. Brand 9 Signs: no.

bullets.title: Google Cloud now co-maintains MCP and Agent Skills under the Linux Foundation's AAIF
bullets.summary: Reported Nov 12 via the Google Open Source Blog: Google Cloud's Kurtis Van Gent is a co-maintainer of MCP and Agent Skills within the Agentic AI Foundation, putting Google alongside Anthropic in stewarding both standards.
bullets.how: The Construct: skills and MCP servers built to the open spec should port across Claude and Gemini, so keep them spec-clean rather than Claude-only. PRAGMA: a cross-vendor standards story for clients worried about lock-in. Brand 9 Signs: no.

praxis_lesson: Treat every tool, MCP server and plugin update as new code: pin versions, gate upgrades and re-review before an unattended loop trusts it, because malicious updates run outside the model's context where prompt-injection defenses can't see them. Once a multi-step tool chain is stable, move it into code (Code Mode, scripts) to cut tokens and shrink what the agent has to be trusted with.
